Thirty comments

Seamus Cooley’s

You’ll find this in a set with the Hole in the Hedge on Martin Hayes’s cd Under the Moon. Nice easy jigs, well-suited for beginners but fun for anyone to play. Also a good lesson in not over ornamenting a melody….

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on December 4th, 2001.

Joe Cooley’s Delight

This one follows the Morning Lark as played by Noel Hill and Tony McMahon. At our session we always add on Tom Billy’s at the end which makes for a nice threesome.

↳ Posted by Bannerman on October 13th, 2003.

Aka Cooley’s

Great tune. I learned this from Noel Hill as Cooley’s jig. Noel and Tony Linnane finish off their live album with this one, and a rousing one it is, too!

Lucy Farr’s

I was looking for the jig which is played in the first part of “The Seagull Jigs” on the “Momentum” album of CrossCurrent (very nice album by the way). It is referred to as Lucy Farr’s, but if you Google that, you will find most of all her barndance, which seems to be very popular, and a few jigs which are sometimes titles Lucy Farr’s jig #1 and Lucy Farr’s jig #2, but which are not the one I was looking for. During my seach I also came accross a jig that I couldn’t find on The Session, but that probably can be found here under another name. I found it on http://www.vashonceltictunes.net/irish/. If it already is on The Session, but with another name, I can probably suppress this post, and have a look at that other entry.

Re: Seamus Cooley’s

I think that the jig version, Seamus Cooley’s, as played by Noel Hill and Tony MacMahon on
Music of Dreams, and the single jig version, Lucy Farr’s , are subtly (or not so subtly) different.
Paddy (Offaly) O’Brien has the single jig, which he calls Lifting the Latch in his tune collection, vol. three.
(His version is essentially the same as X:5 from The Archivist .)
He writes:
Lucy Farr was originally from Ballinakill in Co. Galway. Her maiden name was Lucy Kirwan,
and before she emigrated to London she had already acquired a sizeable number of single jigs
from her fiddle-playing father. This one here is another one from the repertoire of her father
that I heard her play on an old cassette recording.

↳ Posted by ithaca-markb on March 29th, 2026.
